sections.h2: How does selling a house in Bristol work?
sections.html:
Bristol in Bucks County is most often Bristol Township, the large municipality of about 54,000 residents that includes Levittown neighborhoods, Croydon and Bath. A sale there runs through the agreement of sale, a township change of occupancy approval on resale, settlement and a deed recorded with the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds. Bristol Borough is a separate municipality with its own rules, so confirm which one your address falls in.

The township's Building and Planning Department is at 2501 Bath Road and answers questions at 215-785-3680. Most of what follows comes from the township's 2026 fee schedule and permit pages.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Bristol Township's layout and history?
sections.html:
Bristol Township covers 15.84 square miles of land and another 1.27 of water, and its housing mixes postwar subdivisions with older villages near the river. It was formed in 1692 as Buckingham Township and renamed Bristol in 1702. The Delaware Canal arrived in 1831, and the township stayed largely agricultural until the 1950s, when William Levitt began building Levittown in 1952, partly inside its borders.

Named places inside the township include Bath, Croydon, Edgely, Midway, Newportville, Pine Grove and part of Levittown, with Fairless Hills also counted in its neighborhoods. Mill Creek, Neshaminy Creek and Queen Anne Creek run through it. The Phineas Pemberton House, begun in 1687, is on the National Register of Historic Places. Public schools belong to the Bristol Township School District, whose main high school is Harry S. Truman High School.

sections.h2: Which roads and transit connect Bristol Township?
sections.html:
Bristol Township sits at the junction of Interstate 95, the Pennsylvania Turnpike and Interstate 295. Bristol Pike carries US 13 through the township, and Veterans Highway carries PA 413 toward the Burlington-Bristol Bridge.

  • Public roads: 203.47 miles in 2022, with 172.22 miles township-maintained, 27.45 miles under PennDOT and 3.80 miles under the Turnpike Commission.
  • Bus: SEPTA Suburban routes 127, 128 and 129.
  • Rail: SEPTA's Trenton Line stops at Croydon station in the township.

Commutes average 27.4 minutes, and 92.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so few households move in a given year.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Bristol Township homes?
sections.html:
Most Bristol Township homes are owner occupied. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates are below.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 72.4 percent of housing units.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $315,500.
  • Median gross rent: $1,245.
  • Households: 20,908, with a median income of $79,101.

The population was 54,291 in the 2020 census and an estimated 54,063 in July 2025, a dip of half a percent. The climate is humid subtropical, and the wettest day since 1981 delivered 6.42 inches of rain on August 27, 2011, so check basements and sump pumps before showings.

sections.h2: What does the township charge for resale and related fees?
sections.html:
The Resolution 2026-25 fee schedule sets a $100 charge for a residential change of occupancy on resale, and a second inspection costs $40 if one is needed. The table lists the fees most sellers meet.

ItemFee or rate
Residential resale change of occupancy$100
Second inspection, if needed$40
Four-year tax certification$35 ($50 rush)
Sewer certification$50
Lien fee$180
Residential sewer charge$111.03 per quarter
Refuse user fee$400 a year, billed on the tax bill

Source: Bristol Township 2026 fee schedule (Resolution 2026-25). Order the tax and sewer certifications before settlement is scheduled.

sections.h2: How do transfer tax and property tax work in Bristol Township?
sections.html:
The township's fee schedule lists a real estate transfer tax of 1 percent of the purchase price, split 0.5 percent to the township and 0.5 percent to the Bristol Township School District. Add the state's 1 percent and the total on a sale is 2 percent, and the grantor and grantee are jointly liable under state law.

Township millage for 2026 lists these funds: general 16.58 mills, debt 2.45, capital improvement 1.5, fire protection 3, recreation 0.9 and rescue squad 0.55. That adds to 24.98 mills before the school and county rates. A buyer must send contact information to the Bucks County Board of Assessment within 30 days of buying, under Act 29. The board's 2026 annual appeal deadline was August 3, 2026, with a $75 filing fee per parcel, and any change takes effect in the 2027 tax year. Ask the board each year for the next date.

sections.h2: What permits and open work should a Bristol seller check?
sections.html:
Unpermitted work is the common obstacle, because the township doubles permit fees when it finds work done without a permit and may add court fines. Permits are needed for additions, fences, renovations, decks, pools, demolitions and electrical, plumbing and HVAC equipment.

All contractors working in the township must be registered, and registrations run on a calendar year. Before you list, confirm that finals were signed off on past projects. The fee schedule also lists an annual rental fee of $100 for a single-family dwelling and an occupied rental fine of $320, so landlords selling a tenant-occupied house should check their rental status first.

faqs.q: Do I need a use and occupancy inspection to sell a house in Bristol Township?
faqs.a: The township's 2026 fee schedule lists a $100 residential change of occupancy charge on resale and $40 for a second inspection if one is needed. Call 215-785-3680 to confirm the steps for your address.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Bristol Township sale?
faqs.a: The contract sets who pays, but state law makes seller and buyer jointly liable. The total is 2 percent: 1 percent to Pennsylvania, 0.5 percent to the township and 0.5 percent to the school district.

faqs.q: What certifications does the township issue at sale?
faqs.a: Tax and sewer certifications. A four-year tax certification costs $35, or $50 rushed, and a sewer certification costs $50. Order them before settlement is scheduled.

faqs.q: Is Bristol Township the same as Bristol Borough?
faqs.a: No. They are separate municipalities in Bucks County with separate rules and officials. The figures on this page describe the township.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Bristol Township assessment after selling?
faqs.a: Appeals are filed by the aggrieved party of record, and the Bucks County board's 2026 annual deadline was August 3, 2026. Changes from an annual appeal take effect in the 2027 tax year.
